title: Anki-Ready Spaced-Repetition Card Factory
whatYouGet: Atomic, expert-standard spaced-repetition flashcards on any maths topic - pipe-delimited and ready to import straight into the free Anki app, with cloze versions and a first-week review schedule.
howToUse: Name the topic and card count (optionally paste your notes as the source), then copy the pipe-delimited table into a .txt file and import it into Anki.
effectiveUsage: 1. Replace [TOPIC] with a specific chapter (e.g. 'Definite Integration properties, Class 12') and set [CARD COUNT].
2. Optionally paste your own notes or a textbook section under 'Source text' so cards match exactly what you study.
3. Copy the Front | Back | Tag table into a plain text file and import it into Anki (File > Import, field separator: pipe).
4. Hand-write the 3 cards it tells you to make yourself - those are the ones that stick best.
5. Follow the first-week review schedule instead of cramming all cards in one sitting.
commonFix: If cards are too long or compound, reply: 'Split every card that tests more than one fact into separate atomic cards and regenerate the table.'
promptText:
You are a spaced-repetition expert who writes mathematics flashcards to the standard of serious Anki users. Create high-quality cards on [TOPIC] for a [CLASS OR EXAM] student (or from the source text I paste below), aiming for [CARD COUNT] cards.

CONSTRAINTS (apply strictly):
- One fact per card (atomic) - split anything compound.
- Front asks, back is a short precise answer - never a wall of text.
- Prefer 'why / when to use / apply' cards over pure formula-recall wherever the topic allows (e.g. 'When does integration by parts beat substitution?' rather than only 'State the by-parts formula').
- Include formula cards with their conditions of validity on the back (domain, restrictions, special cases).
- Add cloze-deletion versions for key formulas and definitions.
- Avoid yes/no cards and ambiguous fronts.
- If a card would be low-value or untestable, skip it and say which and why.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
A pipe-delimited table ready to paste into Anki:
Front | Back | Tag

Then, after the table:
(a) **Make these by hand** - 3 cards I should write myself, and why they are better self-made.
(b) **First-week review schedule** - when to review the new cards over days 1-7.
(c) **Skipped** - any facts you deliberately left out, with the reason.

Source text (optional):
[PASTE SOURCE]

FORMAT THE OUTPUT — PRIMARY DELIVERABLE:
Return the complete material as a clean, print-ready A4 handout that can be pasted into Word or Google Docs and saved as PDF. Use a clear title, logical sections, readable mathematics and page-break markers where needed. Keep student material separate from the answer key or teacher notes.

promptText:
ROLE: Act as a master exam-strategy coach famous for legitimate, mathematically valid speed shortcuts.

CONTEXT: My [EXAM e.g. JEE Main / NEET] students lose time on [TOPIC e.g. Quadratic Roots / Permutations / Ratio-Proportion]. I want shortcuts that are genuinely valid (not memorised hacks that break) so they can solve under time pressure.

YOUR TASK:
1. Give EXACTLY [NUMBER e.g. 7] speed techniques for [TOPIC] that save real time in the exam.
2. For each trick: state the trick, when it applies, when it FAILS (its limitation), and a worked example solving the same problem the long way AND the fast way.
3. Show the approximate time saved per trick.
4. End with a 1-minute drill of 5 quick questions to practise the tricks, with answers.

INPUT: Here is the topic and the kind of questions students see: [PASTE DETAILS HERE]. If number is blank, use 7. Stay inside this topic.

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: For every trick, prove it works by solving the example BOTH ways and confirming the answers match; that is your verification. Explicitly test one case where the trick could fail to define its limitation. Never present a shortcut as universal if it has exceptions. Never invent formulas or values. Keep maths legible in clean LaTeX or clear plain text.

OUTPUT FORMAT, in this exact order:

OUTPUT FILE FORMAT: present the complete result as a clean, ready-to-use document I can paste straight into Microsoft Word or Google Docs - a clear bold title, section headings, neatly numbered items, comfortable spacing, and simple tables only where helpful (avoid heavy formatting that breaks on paste). It must also print cleanly to PDF on A4 (File > Print > Save as PDF). Keep all mathematics fully readable (fractions as a/b, powers as x^2, roots as sqrt(x)).

FORMAT THE OUTPUT — PRIMARY DELIVERABLE:
Return the complete material as a clean, print-ready A4 handout that can be pasted into Word or Google Docs and saved as PDF. Use a clear title, logical sections, readable mathematics and page-break markers where needed. Keep student material separate from the answer key or teacher notes.


MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.
A. Title block: 'Topic: [TOPIC]', 'Speed Tricks for [EXAM]', 'Compiled by [YOUR NAME]'.
B. SECTION 1 - TRICKS: for each trick, the four parts (What / When it applies / When it fails / Worked example long-way vs fast-way) and time saved.
C. SECTION 2 - PROOF CHECK: one line per trick confirming both methods gave the same answer.
D. SECTION 3 - 1-MINUTE DRILL: 5 quick questions with an answer key.

RULES: Every trick must be mathematically valid with stated limits. Both-method check is mandatory. No invented values. No 'works always' claim unless it truly does.

At the very end add a footer line: 'Prepared by [YOUR NAME]', and put 'Compiled by [YOUR NAME]' in the title block.

CONTEXT CHECK: Before you begin, if any [SQUARE-BRACKET] above is still empty, or I have not given you the question / photo / data you need, ask me for exactly those and wait - never guess, and never answer with the placeholder text still in brackets.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. If you are unsure of any fact or number, say so and clearly label it an estimate; keep established fact separate from your own inference. Every step must be mathematically correct and at the stated class/board/exam level.

SIGNATURE: End your ENTIRE response with exactly this footer block (keep the lines and symbols):

title: Common JEE Traps in a Chapter (Mistake-Proofing Guide)
whatYouGet: A guide to the exact traps a chapter hides, with the wrong vs right working side by side.
howToUse: Name the chapter, paste the prompt, and get the top traps with wrong-vs-right worked examples.
effectiveUsage: Open any AI chat.
Type the chapter name.
Paste the prompt and send.
Use the wrong-vs-right pairs in class.
Give the trap-checklist before tests.
For a trustworthy answer key: paste the finished paper into a FRESH chat and ask it to solve and grade it as an unseen exam (it catches its own slips).
commonFix: If a 'trap' is not really a common mistake, reply: "Trap 2 is rare in practice - replace it with a genuinely frequent JEE mistake in this chapter and show the wrong-vs-right working."
